name: Hard and Soft Depth Regularization
definition: A regularization strategy that constrains 3D Gaussian geometry by encouraging spatial reshaping (movement of centers) rather than deforming Gaussian shapes, preventing detail loss and blurred appearance caused by forcing anisotropic Gaussians to fit smooth monocular depth.
summary: Hard and Soft Depth Regularization prevents detail loss in 3D Gaussian Splatting by freezing shape parameters during optimization, allowing primitives to reshuffle spatially rather than deform.
